title: Where is the angle when someone swings?
description: A child on a swing goes faster when the swing starts from a greater angle, but no angle is drawn. One arm is fixed at the starting position and the other is drawn to the highest position on one side, and the angle between them is seen.
teaching_notes: One idea: an angle can be seen in a motion, between the starting position and the highest position on one side. Watch for students who look for a drawn angle and say there is none.

source: Figure it Out: Where are the angles?, Q3
video_script.why: The child finds an angle that is not drawn, by fixing one arm and drawing the other, as the solved example did for the clock hands.
video_script.substitution: The swing of the book's question, with the starting position and the highest position on one side.
video_script.anchor: Ruhee on a swing, drawn from the side with the fixed hanging point above
video_script.payoff_line: The angle lies between the starting position and the greatest swing on one side

final_answer.value: the angle is between the starting position and the greatest swing on one side
final_answer.spoken: between the starting position and the greatest swing on one side

names.Ruhee: book character who enjoys a swing and notices that a greater starting angle gives a greater speed

maths_rules: one arm is fixed at the position where the swing starts, the initial position
the other arm is drawn to the position where the swing reaches its greatest swing on one side
the angle lies between these two arms, and a greater angle goes with a greater speed
video_script.design: The swing stays on the board. One arm is fixed at the starting position and a second arm is drawn to the highest position, and the words greatest swing are held back until the answer line.
open_questions: The book says the angle lies between the starting position and the greatest swing on one side, but does not name the vertex. The video lets both arms start from the fixed point where the swing hangs, which is an inference.
